items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: I told Ralph the other day, it begins with K. from uptown.

ctx.x: Bud Scott on the guitar. And Bud Scott stayed with him practically until his band broke up. The Robichaud was a left-handed violin player. Old John Robichaud. And he had... He had two Kimballs in his band, you know. He had one called Henry Kimball, that was his bass player. And Andrew Kimball. The trumpet player. Andrew Kimball and Henry Kimball. And Henry Kimball is still active playing now. He plays baseball and he's a... He's a... a... a...
a... a... Yeah. Well, I've been trying to think for three days of a trumpet player. I told Ralph the other day, it begins with K. from uptown. It went through my head. Keelan. Frank Keelan?

Frank Keelan was a trumpet player. With this one of these old... You know, like you ever heard him, I guess you would call it a barrel house. You know. That's a barrel house. That's a barrel house. That's a barrel house. Yeah. Well, he didn't play in all these good time, big time bands, you know. But all those bands like we were like... I had one time when we was playing up at Tom Anderson. When I worked at Tom Anderson, he played... He played trumpet in there, because he... It was... He played soft trumpet, you…
